name_zh: 相位与动作幅度的可识别分解
formal_object: A smooth legal trajectory Y(t), small phase offsets tau in a fixed endpoint-preserving basis, amplitude basis B; desired model/input-derived residual r; P is the phase Jacobian.

operations.condition: Smooth trajectory and small monotone time warp

operations.input: Weighted least squares in phase and amplitude blocks
operations.condition: Unconstrained phase elimination only when no phase inequality is active

operations.input: Overlap of phase and amplitude spans
operations.condition: Jacobian rank and gauge are checked

derivation_steps.statement: Linearize the repair as r approximately P xi+B gamma, with phase endpoint offsets zero.
derivation_steps.justification: Taylor expansion in a declared small phase basis.

derivation_steps.statement: Let M=I-P(P^T W P)^dagger P^T W; after unconstrained phase elimination, gamma*=(B^T W M B+lambda I)^-1 B^T W M r.
derivation_steps.justification: Weighted Schur elimination and ridge least squares.

derivation_steps.statement: For monotone time, impose 1+tau'(t)>0; if the bound is active, solve the full constrained block problem instead of the unconstrained formula.
derivation_steps.justification: Elimination formula does not silently enforce inequality constraints.

derivation_steps.statement: Overlapping phase/amplitude directions are unidentifiable without extra constraints; residual second-order error is O(||tau||^2).
derivation_steps.justification: Rank deficiency and the retained Taylor remainder limit the claim.

assumptions: Time warp is internal to the method; output is still evaluated at every original benchmark timestamp, with untouched references.
Phase targets use legal input/model evidence and no confirmation labels.
Endpoints, monotonicity, derivative regularity and interpolation error are checked; positive amplitude ridge lambda>0 ensures the profiled inverse is defined.
Input evidence may not distinguish timing from amplitude; then this is an identifiability boundary rather than a successful repair.
method_expression: Jointly infer a small anchored monotone phase correction and amplitude correction; use the profiled formula only in the unconstrained phase regime; render outputs at original times.
distinguishing_prediction: Timing-dominated errors should respond to phase correction while amplitude-only shrinkage loses motion; amplitude-dominated errors should show the opposite pattern.
falsifier: Reject if ordinary lag/alignment with equal evidence/budget is sufficient, or phase/amplitude remains unidentifiable on the native task.
closest_alternative: Classical phase-amplitude registration and Schur projection; simple lag correction, smoothing and displacement scaling.
decisive_comparison: Base, phase-only, amplitude-only and joint constrained repair with equal fitting/call budget; native CD-M/3D/4D at untouched timestamps and fresh confirmation.
operational_delta: Separates two competing mechanisms instead of interpreting every motion mismatch as coordinate noise; classical registration remains prior art.
feasibility_and_cost: Requires a qualified input/model motion target and a bounded nonlinear solve; target access and native method timing remain unresolved.
algebra_review_basis: Checked the Schur formula, active-inequality exception, nonidentifiability and second-order remainder. No relabeling of evaluation time.
empirical_status: Not implemented in this round; no native method comparison or outcome.
originality_status: Unadjudicated. Classical tools and historical related code are explicitly attributed.
